questions.text:
Consider the following declaration:
 int a, *b=&a, **c=&b;
The following program fragment
 a=4;    **c=5;
questions.solution:
c points to b and b points to a, so **c is a itself. **c = 5 sets a = 5.

Answer: assigns 5 to a

options: does not change the value of a
assigns address of c to a

questions.text: If n has  3, then the statement a[++n]=n++;
questions.solution:
n is modified twice (++n and n++) in one statement without a sequence point. This is undefined behaviour in C, so the result depends on the compiler.

Answer: what is assigned is compiler dependent

questions.text:
Consider the following program fragment
 if(a > b)  if(b > c)     s1;  else s2;
s2 will be executed if
questions.solution:
The else pairs with the nearest if, i.e. if (b [latex]\gt[/latex] c). So s2 runs when a [latex]\gt[/latex] b is true and b [latex]\gt[/latex] c is false.

Answer: a [latex]\gt[/latex] b and b [latex]\le[/latex] c
